title: Hawaii ex parte renewal share, August 2026
question: What will CMS first publish as Hawaii's August 2026 original (O) submission ex parte renewal share, calculated as 100 times beneficiaries renewed on an ex parte basis divided by beneficiaries due for renewal, without seasonal adjustment, rounded to one decimal?
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolves to Hawaii's ex parte renewal share for the August 2026 reporting period, computed from the original (O) submission row in CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c when CMS first publishes it. Calculate 100 times Beneficiaries Whose Coverage Was Renewed on an Ex Parte Basis (Metric 5a1) divided by Beneficiaries with a Renewal Due (Metric 5), using the numerator and denominator as first published, rounded to one decimal. Subsequent updated (U) submissions and revisions do not alter resolution.
drivers: Ex parte processing and reporting classification

reasoning.text: Hawaii August 2026 original-submission ex parte renewal share

The target is Hawaii's state row for reporting period 202608 in dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c, original submission O, resolved on its first official publication. CMS's snapshot table defines the ex parte rate as a percentage of all beneficiaries due for renewal: 100 times Metric 5a1 / Metric 5. This is a raw state-cohort rate, not a national total or weighted interstate average.

History-access limitation: the exact count-derived Hawaii O-row history could not be fetched through the official CSV or API with the web tool. The 13 historical observations instead come from CMS's published monthly original-report snapshot state tables. They use the same renewal-outcome variant and denominator, excluding quarterly updated outcomes, but are rounded to whole percentages, with up to 0.5 percentage point rounding error. They are not presented as exact one-decimal count-derived shares.

reasoning.call: Fetched June, July and August 2025 CMS snapshot PDFs listed in sourceContext; opened their Coverage Retention and Disenrollment Rates by State tables.
reasoning.result: Hawaii original-report ex parte rates: June 2025 85%, July 2025 86%, August 2025 77%. Corresponding beneficiaries due for renewal: 36,856; 36,119; 36,003.

reasoning.result: Hawaii original-report ex parte rates: September 2025 69%, October 2025 77%, November 2025 74%, December 2025 72%. Corresponding beneficiaries due: 40,547; 38,684; 36,753; 40,422.

reasoning.call: Fetched January through March 2026 CMS snapshot PDFs listed in sourceContext; opened their Coverage Retention and Disenrollment Rates by State tables.
reasoning.result: Hawaii original-report ex parte rates: January 2026 69%, February 2026 57%, March 2026 65%. Corresponding beneficiaries due: 26,831; 18,463; 23,602.

reasoning.call: Fetched April through June 2026 CMS snapshot PDFs listed in sourceContext; opened their Coverage Retention and Disenrollment Rates by State tables.
reasoning.result: Hawaii original-report ex parte rates: April 2026 70%, May 2026 71%, June 2026 74%. Corresponding beneficiaries due: 26,046; 38,958; 36,142. June also reports 88% total renewed and 3% pending.

reasoning.text: The outside-view reference class is the 13 consecutive Hawaii monthly original-report observations from June 2025 through June 2026. Their unweighted mean base rate is 72.7692%; the latest observation is 74%. This anchors the forecast before adjustments.

Level: favor persistence near June with weak shrinkage toward the historical mean. Momentum: the recovery from February to June does not establish sustained positive drift, so no separate trend increment is applied. One-off: retain February's low in the dispersion estimate rather than assume it cannot recur. Policy mechanism: no fetched evidence establishes a discrete August Hawaii processing change, so apply no policy increment. One prior August observation is insufficient to estimate a stable seasonal effect.

Prior/update/interval: use a persistence prior with weak mean reversion, based on the 13 fetched rounded original-report observations. Point = 0.75*74 + 0.25*72.7692 = 73.6923%, rounded to 73.7%; separate momentum, one-off, seasonal and policy adjustments are zero. The 12 successive changes are [1,-9,-8,8,-3,-2,-3,-12,8,5,1,3] percentage points, with mean -0.9167 and centered squared sum 464.9167. Sample sigma = 6.5012 percentage points = sqrt(464.9167/11). The one-month normal 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 8.3215 points. For the two-month June-to-August horizon, multiply by sqrt(2), assuming independent monthly innovations: half-width = 11.7684 points. Bounds = 73.6923 +/- 11.7684 = [61.9239,85.4607], rounded to [61.9,85.5]. Coverage is approximate because cohort seasonality, dependent changes and snapshot rounding may violate the model assumptions.

Publication-date verification limitation: the official CMS snapshot archive fetched this run lists June 2026 released September 25, 2026, May released August 28, and April released July 31. It does not announce the August 2026 publication date. The required official verification of December 15, 2026 could not be completed. resolutionDate remains the ledger-specified 2026-12-15; it is not asserted to be a verified CMS release date, and no date is inferred from cadence.

Upside risk: a cohort especially amenable to automatic renewal or improved matching could raise the share; a return to July 2025's published 86% would land above the interval. Downside risk: a difficult verification cohort, processing disruption or reclassification toward renewal forms could depress the share; February 2026's published 57% would land below the interval. Either recurrence would be outside the interval.
